MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 21, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:01 p.m., on October 21, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on October 18, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  Council Member Ury

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager /Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness

CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that it is not necessary to discuss the item that was placed
on the agenda for Closed Session so the Council may simply recess until the 6:00 hour.

City Council Minutes  1  October 21, 2013
 RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim November 6, 2013, To Be "National Eating Healthy Day"

  Mayor Reardon presented the proclamation to Business Development Director Shelly
  Belland from the American Heart Association.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bill Chase, M.V.: stated that there is a parking problem in his neighborhood and the requirement
to leave 15 feet clearance from a fire hydrant makes it illegal for cars to park in front of many
homes. He requested that it be legal for vehicles to park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant with
violators receiving a warning notice, followed by a citation. Mr. Chase also reported that an
unlicensed contractor on his street works late at night using power tools and playing loud music.

James Copeland, M.V.: announced that he has been watching his neighborhood deteriorate over
the last few years. There are multiple families living in homes, cars speeding on the street,
garbage cans left out to save parking spaces, and 2nd hand smoke coming from a neighbor's
home. He asked the City and the Sheriff's Department to assist with these matters.

Dennis Lumley, M.V.: invited the Council and residents to honor Veterans Day at the Elks
Lodge on Tuesday, November 5, 2013, at 7:00 p.m.

F.K. (Joe) Holtzman, M.V.: announced that more than 700 homeowners have gone solar and we
are getting close to energy independence in Mission Viejo. He also discussed his attendance at a
recent symposium on the decommissioning of San Onofre and he outlined the dangers of the
toxic waste stored at the nuclear plant. Mr. Holtzman asked city officials to attend an upcoming
meeting regarding waste storage management at the Sheraton in Carlsbad on November 19.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that he is still waiting to meet with the City's Chief of Police
to discuss cost savings ideas and he noted that the Sheriff's Department has over $1 billion in
unfunded pension liability. Mr. Wontrobski informed the Council that the OCERS Board
recently adopted a resolution addressing antagonistic or disrespectful responses during public
comments and he recommended that the City Council consider adopting something similar.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4 and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

City Council Minutes  2  October 21, 2013
 Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ury

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of October 7, 2013, as presented.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2013

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2013

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August
  2013

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for August 2013

  Received and filed.

10. Fleet Motorcycle Maintenance Services

  (1) Awarded a Contract to Huntington Beach Honda in the amount of $105,000 for the Police
  Services Motorcycle Maintenance Program for the term beginning October 22, 2013, to June
  30, 2015, and; (2) approved a Purchase Order to Huntington Beach Honda in the amount of
  $45,000 for FY 2013-2014.
City Council Minutes  3  October 21, 2013
 11. Orange County Transportation Authority 2013-2014 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  Adopted Resolution 13-57 Approving the Submittal of the La Paz Road Corridor
  Improvement Project to the Orange County Transportation Authority for Funding Under
  the Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program
  (Project P).

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

12. Ordinance Pertaining to Public Cost Recovery for Multiple Calls to Disruptive
  Gatherings

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Dave Stefanides, Orange County Association of Realtors, Laguna Hills: expressed concern
  about the lien process for an owner who has tenants, not only at multi-family units but also
  in single family homes.

  Tommy Thompson, California Apartment Association, Irvine: thanked the City Attorney
  for doing a fantastic job of explaining the ordinance. He stated that he supports the way it
  is headed and he offered discuss the ordinance with city officials if necessary.

  Ed Sachs, M.V.: asked the Council to vote against the ordinance since California Penal
  Code 415 already covers disturbance of the peace.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to introduce
  Ordinance 13-299, as amended, Adding Chapter 11.23 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Regarding Public Cost Recovery for Multiple Calls to Disruptive
  Gatherings.

  Amendments: Add a new section 11.23.030(e) and change fifteen days to thirty days in
  section 11.23.030(c).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ury

City Council Minutes  4  October 21, 2013
 RECESS

At the hour of 7:49 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
8:00 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ury was absent.)

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Road Closure Request from Trabuco Hills High School Instrumental Music Booster
  Club

  Mike Feldman, M.V.: asked for the City's assistance with a parking plan for the upcoming
  band competition at Trabuco Hills High School.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  approve the Special Events Permit submitted by the Trabuco Hills High School
  Instrumental Music Booster Club authorizing the closure of Mustang Run between Los
  Alisos and Aguilar on Saturday, November 16, 2013, subject to the City helping the school
  with a traffic plan.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

NEW BUSINESS

13. Consideration of City Council and Successor Agency Resolutions Approving
  Agreement to Re-Establish Loan Pursuant to Section 34191.4 between the City and
  the Successor Agency Following the Obtaining of a Finding of Completion

  Special Counsel Celeste Brady, Stradling Yocca Carlson and Rauth, presented the
  staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to adopt City
  Council Resolution 13-58 Approving Agreement to Re-Establish Loan Pursuant to Section
  34191.4 between the City of Mission Viejo and the Successor Agency to the Mission Viejo
  Community Development Agency.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  October 21, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to adopt Successor
  Agency Resolution 13-06 Approving Agreement to Re-Establish Loan Pursuant to Section
  34191.4 between the City of Mission Viejo and the Successor Agency to the Mission Viejo
  Community Development Agency; Directing Submittal of such Loan Agreement to the
  Oversight Board to Consider that the Loan Agreement Was for Legitimate Redevelopment
  Purposes; and Making other Findings in Connection Therewith.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

14. Cal Card Program and Activity

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that OCFA conducted an audit of their CAL Card
  program. He provided the City Clerk with a copy of the audit and recommended that staff
  review it to see if the same problems exist with the City's program.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, receive
  the staff report and provide direction to staff.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to
  direct staff to come back to the City Council with information on performing an audit of the
  Cal Card program and to provide a potential scope of work and the cost.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

City Council Minutes  6  October 21, 2013
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)

3.  Check Register Dated September 27, 2013 in the Amount of $987,346.92

  Council Member Schlicht asked for more information on the Discovery Science Center Eco
  Challenge program (page 8 on the check register) and expressed concern that the City is
  giving funds to different programs that appear to be outside of the City.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

4.  Check Register Dated October 4, 2013 in the Amount of $2,372,359.49

  Council Member Schlicht, referring to page 8, asked for an explanation of the payment to
  Johnson-Frank and Associates for property line review on Aldeano.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to ratify
  the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ury

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

15. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed procurement irregularities at the OCFA and stated
  that a variety of agencies and news outlets are investigating the matter. He provided the
  City Clerk with copies of letters he has written on the subject, as well as letters he wrote to
  the OCFA Board of Directors regarding his own wage cost study.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  October 21, 2013
 16. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon read a summary of the recent Foothill/Eastern TCA meeting which Mayor
  Pro Tem Kelley attended on her behalf.

17. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon announced that she was unable to attend the recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA.

18. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Manager Wilberg notified the Council that he received a call from the Superintendent of the
Saddleback Unified School District who informed him that the District has received complaints
about people distributing literature at back to school nights at various school campuses and the
district has restrictions against that.

City Attorney’s Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

Council Member Leckness shared a short video on the City’s smoke alarm program. Residents
can call (949) 470-3017 and OCFA will send someone to test their alarms. If necessary, a new
smoke alarm will be installed free of charge. Council Member Leckness also discussed his
attendance at the City’s 3rd annual campout on Saturday. He stated that it was a great community
event, with over 600 attendees, and he commended the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for
providing the food. Council Member Leckness enjoyed seeing the families spending time

City Council Minutes  8  October 21, 2013
 together and he shared the story of a little boy who was overjoyed to ride on a golf cart and the
couple he met who were camping, for the first time, with their 2 month-old baby girl.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at a recent symposium on the
decommissioning of SONGS. She stated that the watchdog group is pushing for an independent
public evaluation of the decommissioning and the CPUC has accepted them as an intervener.
Council Member Schlicht noted that it is up to the CPUC, as well as this watchdog group, to
make sure that SCE spends the $4 billion decommissioning budget to properly and faithfully
clean up the waste at SONGS. She also noted that the NEC’s role is safety and it appears that
they too will accept this group as a citizens’ oversight panel. Council Member Schlicht stated
that the main problem is that the federal government has failed to come up with a depository plan
and it looks like the nuclear waste will be held at San Onofre for another 60 years if it is not
transferred elsewhere. She stated that this is happening all across the nation, not just here in
Orange County. In honor of the people who attend the Council Meetings and watch from home,
Council Member Schlicht ended with a quote from Andrew Jackson, the 7th United States
President: “But you must remember, my fellow-citizens, that eternal vigilance by the people is
the price of liberty, and that you must pay the price if you wish to secure the blessing.”

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury was absent.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley commended the City Manager and City staff for a very successful Walk
Against Drugs and Emergency Preparedness Expo. She gave special thanks to Tammy
Descoteaux, Paula Monical, Khatra Hashemeyan, Paul Catsimanes, the entire Police Services
department, as well as Orange County Supervisors Pat Bates and Todd Spitzer. The event began
at Mission Viejo High School with Mayor Reardon and the City’s new Police Chief giving
excellent speeches, and the guest speaker was wheelchair tennis champion David Wagner. She
Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that it was inspiring to see the participants listening to the message
about saying no to drugs and walking up La Paz to the emergency preparedness expo. This year
the Rock ‘N Road’s battle of the bands joined in the very successful day and she reiterated her
thanks to staff for the great preparation and for then turning around and putting on the City’s
annual campout. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley outlined her attendance at the Nadadores annual
meeting where she heard really good results of the program and Coach Rose expressed the
Nadadores’ appreciation for the partnership with the City of Mission Viejo. She also announced
that she and Mayor Reardon attended the screening of this month’s character movie, Bully. It
was very shocking to hear that bullying is growing and she encouraged parents to listen to their
kids, stay involved and to know what is going on. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley outlined upcoming
events including Hometown Halloween on October 26 at the Norman P. Murray Community
Center from 4:00 to 8:00 p.m. and the Wheelchair Tennis Masters from November 5-11 at the
City Council Minutes  9  October 21, 2013
 Marguerite Tennis Pavilion. This is the first time that this International tournament will be
hosted in the United States and she encouraged everyone to attend. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem
Kelley recited a quote from the respect newsletter by Herbert Henry Lehman “I must respect the
opinions of others, even if I disagree with them.”

Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon echoed the positive comments about the Walk Against Drugs. She remarked on
the huge crowd of people wearing red shirts and that there were more participants at the
Emergency Preparedness event this year than in previous years. She also announced that an
agent with the DEA has been extremely instrumental in working on cases to ferret out dirty
doctors. He recently built a case against a Doctor Yee who was writing illegal prescriptions at
the Starbucks on Chrisanta. Mayor Reardon noted the scary reality that the doctor was issuing
the prescriptions across the street from Mission Viejo High School but he was finally convicted
and will be serving 11 years in jail. Mayor Reardon commended Chief Brad NewMyer for doing
a great job on his speech at the Walk Against Drugs and she discussed her attendance at a drug
trends event on October 9 with a panel of parents and young people. The City’s own Diana
Presta has volunteered her time and taken on a leadership role to communicate the issue of drug
abuse in Mission Viejo and her son Andrew, who is celebrating over a year of recovery, also
participated. Mayor Reardon stated that it is very interesting to listen to parents and the young
people who are now in recovery and she observed the difference in the kids’ view of their
parents when they were addicted and how they view their parents now. Mayor Reardon
announced that she and Mayor Pro Tem Kelley attended a Casta del Sol Republican Club
meeting where former State Senator Mimi Walters gave an update on what’s going on in
Sacramento and she stated that none of it is good. She also attended the presentation of the
movie Bully which she found extremely troubling and disturbing. Lastly, Mayor Reardon
reminded residents of the Mission for the Armed Forces football game on Friday, October 25 at
Mission Viejo High School, the Elks Club Veterans Day ceremony on November 5, and she
announced that NEGU will collect toys for Joy Jars at the upcoming Santa’s arrival event.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:57 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Tom Goodall, to Monday, November 4,
2013, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 18, 2013

City Council Minutes  10  October 21, 2013
